selection_rationale: Use the literature-reported approximately 0.5 s birth period as the common pre-evolution baseline for isolated and recycled comparison tracks.
Adopt a 45 degree baseline inclination so the dipole torque is active without assuming either perfect alignment or orthogonality.
Use the review-reported 10^12 G normal-pulsar field, converted to 10^8 T, to represent the isolated-pulsar baseline.
Choose the effective coefficient so a 10^8 T, 0.5 s, 45 degree pulsar has an order-10^-15 period derivative; unresolved radius, inertia, and electromagnetic constants remain absorbed in this proxy.
Use a modest ten-percent wind-torque contribution as a sensitivity baseline while preserving dipole braking as the dominant isolated mechanism.
Use the review-reported order-10^7 yr inclination-evolution timescale converted to seconds.
No compatible scalar survived extraction; adopt 6.3e14 kg/s as an explicit sub-Eddington sensitivity baseline for steady recycling rather than as a measured rate.
Set the reduced spin-up coefficient to permit substantial but finite period reduction over a 10 Myr accretion interval; it is an effective torque proxy, not a microphysical constant.
Adopt a 10 Myr active recycling interval so the 100 Myr run retains a distinct post-accretion spin-down phase.
Use the reported approximately 100 Myr radio-pulsar lifetime as the integration horizon.
Use 10^-22 s/s as a permissive numerical detectability floor to stop effectively inactive tracks without truncating ordinary pulsar evolution.
Use 5000 tracks as a computationally bounded first-pass population sample large enough for stable distribution summaries.
